label: first copy step after <DEL> when the first original token is t (L>=6)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx == 1), where the fed-back input is the first original token, and only when that token is t. It is silent for L <= 5 (L=5 yields only a few weak hits) and the rate goes up with L, so it is strongest at L=8-9. Top activations come when the sequence starts t t. It does not fire during the original phase (apart from rare weak hits on a t at the last original position), on the <DEL> step, or on later copy steps, and almost never at recall_idx 1 when the first token is not t (a few weak hits on u, digits and g at L=9).

issues: One minor wording error: 'its rate goes up with L' is wrong if rate means how often it fires. Precision of (recall_idx==1)&(in_tok==t)&(L==k) is 0.996, 1.0, 1.0 and 1.0 for L=6..9, so whenever the predicate is true it fires almost every time at every L. What grows with L is the activation size: share of activation mass is 0.10/0.23/0.31/0.35 for L=6..9 on similar step counts (2665-3059). So 'strongest at L=8-9' holds for magnitude, but not for firing rate.
L=5 is silent as claimed: the same predicate with L==5 has precision 0.019.

Test misses are scattered noise. There are 349 missed active steps holding 0.2% of activation mass, all weak (0.01-0.06 of max) at recall_idx 1 with first tokens other than t (o, p, q, u). There are 16 false positives, all at L=6 when the first token is t. Neither forms a class worth a new predicate.
Profile matches the explanation: copy phase holds 100% of activation mass, all at recall_idx 1 (step L+1) and after a <DEL> input; 28 tiny hits fall at orig_idx 8; nothing fires on the <DEL> step.
The 't t' top-activation claim was not separately checked; it does not affect the label.
